findings.title: GET /books query filtering incorrect (id, title/author/isbn, synopsis, q)
findings.detail: Filters applied incorrectly: id filter works but other filters are applied cumulatively with flawed logic; 'q' parameter is treated as a field lookup instead of generic search across title, author, isbn, synopsis; multiple filters are not combined correctly (AND logic is broken). Query parameter validation works but filter parsing mishandles empty results and lacks proper case‑insensitive substring matching across multiple fields.

findings.title: GET /books ordering not guaranteed
findings.detail: Books returned are not sorted by id as required; insertion order may not reflect id order.

findings.title: Filter combination AND logic flawed
findings.detail: When id filter is applied, subsequent filters are applied on the filtered set, but the break statement when books becomes empty stops later filters, causing inconsistent behavior.

findings.title: q parameter not implemented correctly
findings.detail: q should search across title, author, isbn, synopsis; current code treats q as a field lookup, which fails.

findings.title: Minor: missing handling for empty synopsis defaults
findings.detail: Synopsis defaults to empty string; current code copies synopsis from request; fine.

findings.title: GET /books filtering broken (q parameter and general logic)
findings.detail: q parameter searches across fields but code uses b["q"].lower() which does not exist; filter logic does not correctly intersect multiple query parameters; results are not sorted by id.

findings.title: GET /books query parameter validation insufficient
findings.detail: Allows multiple matching filter keys but does not enforce that all supplied query parameters are known; already checks but implementation may still misapply.

findings.title: Missing id reuse after delete handling (not required per spec)
findings.detail: Server reuses ids after delete; spec says id never reused after delete – but implementation never deletes, so fine.

findings.title: PUT /books expects id in path but does not validate it's integer
findings.detail: Path parsing uses int conversion; okay but could be clearer; fine.

findings.title: Incorrect handling of 'q' query parameter
findings.detail: The 'q' parameter is treated as a filter on the same field name 'q', causing KeyError. It should perform case‑insensitive substring matching on any of title, author, isbn, or synopsis, and all applied filters must still be conjunctions.

findings.title: Id reuse after deletion
findings.detail: The server increments next_id on each create, so if a book is later deleted and another is created, the same id may be reused. The requirement is that ids are never reused after a delete.

findings.title: Query q parameter filter implementation error
findings.detail: The q filter treats 'q' as a field name, causing KeyError. Need to implement q as OR search across title, author, isbn, synopsis ignoring case; also ensure multiple filters work correctly.

findings.title: ID path conversion error
findings.detail: GET /books/<id> uses int(path.split('/')[-1]) which raises ValueError if id is not an integer; returns 404 instead of 400 per spec.

findings.title: Filtering logic for multiple query parameters
findings.detail: The current implementation applies filters sequentially; should ensure all applied filters are satisfied (AND). This works in practice but could be clearer; minor clarity issue.

findings.title: PUT/DELETE path parsing: empty ID segment causes ValueError
findings.detail: When path is \'/books/\' (no ID), int(path.split(\"/\")[-1]) raises ValueError. Unlike GET which catches this, PUT/DELETE would crash instead of returning 404.

findings.title: Error response lacks distinction between error types
findings.detail: All errors return generic JSON with 'error' field; no differentiation between validation errors (400) and not-found (404).
